before.label: Before-design dependencies
before.description: DocumentBefore holds optional references directly to Preview, CharacterCount, and SaveButton and writes their UI state.
before.caption: DocumentBefore is the domain class; Preview, CharacterCount, and SaveButton are UI classes. Each arrow is a direct reference to an optional widget (0..1). UI widgets and presentation rules tend to change more often than the domain model, so domain classes should avoid these dependencies.

roles.label: Observer pattern role diagram
roles.description: Subject holds zero or more Observers and calls update(text). ConcreteSubject inherits the registration mechanism from Subject and owns the changing state. ConcreteObserver implements Observer and owns its reaction.

solution.label: Observer solution dependencies
solution.description: Document inherits Subject. Subject holds references through the Observer interface. Preview, CharacterCount, and SaveButton each implement Observer. Document has no direct references to those concrete UI classes.
solution.caption: Document is the concrete Subject. Preview, CharacterCount, and SaveButton are concrete Observers. The domain depends on the Observer contract; UI classes implement that contract and own their presentation rules.

cards.title: Extend the views
cards.text: Add an Observer and register it; keep the Subject's notification logic.

cards.title: Trace indirect calls
cards.text: Find registration sites as well as notification sites when debugging.

cards.title: Choose runtime policies
cards.text: Detachment, failure, ordering, repeated updates, and reentrancy need decisions.

cards.title: A good fit
cards.text: A document model with optional, independently evolving views.

cards.title: A simpler alternative
cards.text: One fixed collaborator can often be called directly.

cards.title: Beyond this pattern
cards.text: Reliable delivery across processes needs transport and delivery policies.

cards.title: Context
cards.text: Several independent objects must react when one object changes, and they come and go at runtime.

cards.title: Problem
cards.text: A changing object that updates its dependents directly knows every concrete dependent and its rules.

cards.title: Solution
cards.text: A Subject notifies registered Observers through one update contract; each Concrete Observer owns its reaction.

cards.title: Consequences
cards.text: Dependents are added without editing the Subject, at the cost of indirect control flow and lifecycle policies.
